newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL palm oil ends mostly up after choppy day.
newsitem.headline: KL palm oil ends mostly up after choppy day.

text.p: PALM OIL FUTURES PALM OIL PHYSICAL

PALM OIL FUTURES - Prices drifted uncertainly in choppy trade before closing mostly higher. Underlying fundamentals remain good but players were mixed over next week's trend. April futures contract is likely to trade between 1,300 and 1,335 next week.
PALM OIL PHYSICAL- Lack of news affected market liquidity. The market was firm and confined to selective nearby CPOs.
The market was closed from February 6 to February 11 for the Chinese Lunar New Year and Moslem Eid al-Fitr.
Malaysia's Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority (PORLA) has postponed its January palm oil stock/export/output data to February 22 from February 15.
Crop forecaster Ivan Wong who normally releases his report on the 14th of every month has decided to postpone the data to next week.
"We are waiting for all these delayed reports before taking fresh positions next week," the dealer added.

"The market was choppy and people preferred to take some profits at current levels in the absence of any supportive news," a trader said, adding that players were mostly sidelined while awaiting a clear trend.
Traders have mixed views over the trend in the near-term. Some said prices will remain steady due to the good fundamentals while others said that the market needs a correction as prices are too high.
The futures market saw gains in most contracts except for expiring spot February futures which shed one ringgit to 1,347 ringgit, they said.
